working_title: The evening routine that was really a work problem

exercise.instructions: You are going to read an article about someone trying to improve their evening routine. Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A–G the one which fits each gap (37)–(42). There is one extra sentence which you do not need to use.
exercise.text_title: The evening routine that was really a work problem
exercise.passage_with_gaps:
I had always believed that a perfect evening routine would solve my persistent tiredness. So, I meticulously planned my evenings, thinking this would finally bring some rest. (37) However, even after arranging everything from a calming herbal tea to a relaxing book, I found myself still feeling drained.

Initially, I thought the solution lay in changing my surface habits. I tried everything from dimming the lights to listening to soothing music. (38) Yet, despite these efforts, I realised I was still mentally checking my work emails and thinking about unfinished tasks.

The realisation struck me one evening when I was interrupted by a message from a colleague. It was then that I noticed how I had never really stopped working. (39) This interruption was a wake-up call, making me aware that my evenings were still dominated by work thoughts.

Determined to change this, I decided to introduce a clear end-of-work ritual. I began writing down the first task for the next day and physically putting away my work materials. (40) This simple act marked a boundary between my work life and personal time.

At first, I was tempted to break this new rule. The thought of checking emails or finishing a task was hard to resist. (41) But I reminded myself of the importance of this boundary, and gradually, I started to notice a shift.

My evenings slowly began to feel different. I could focus more on leisure activities without the constant pull of work. (42) While I can't say this change improved my sleep dramatically, it certainly made my evenings more enjoyable.

Reflecting on this experience, I realised that the key was not in crafting the perfect evening routine. Instead, it was about creating a clear separation between work and personal time. This discovery was personal, and I understood that what worked for me might not be a universal solution.

sentence_pool.A: I realised that I had been carrying my work into my evenings without even noticing.
sentence_pool.B: I had hoped these changes would help me unwind and relax.
sentence_pool.C: Instead of finding peace, I was still preoccupied with work tasks.
sentence_pool.D: This new practice helped me mentally close the door on my workday.
sentence_pool.E: Evenings were meant to be a time to unwind, not to continue working.
sentence_pool.F: This was a crucial turning point in my understanding of the problem.
sentence_pool.G: Over time, the urge to check my work emails decreased.

questions.rationale: The sentence "I had hoped these changes would help me unwind and relax." logically follows the detailed description of the planned evening routine, setting up the expectation that the narrator believed this would solve their tiredness.

The sentence "Instead of finding peace, I was still preoccupied with work tasks." contrasts with the previous sentence about trying various relaxing activities, highlighting the failure of these attempts.

The sentence "This was a crucial turning point in my understanding of the problem." fits here as it marks the realisation that work was still intruding into personal time, which is a significant discovery in the narrative.
The sentence "This new practice helped me mentally close the door on my workday." logically follows the description of the new ritual, explaining its effect on the narrator's mindset.

The sentence "Over time, the urge to check my work emails decreased." fits here as it describes the gradual effect of maintaining the new boundary, which aligns with the narrator's efforts to resist breaking the rule.

The sentence "I realised that I had been carrying my work into my evenings without even noticing." reflects on the change in experience, connecting the shift in evening atmosphere to the earlier realisation.
